explanation: Coins from the mines of Joachimsthal (modern Jáchymov) in Bohemia were called joachimsthalers, then thalers. English turned the name into dollar, and Spanish silver dollars later carried the word around the world.

claims.text: The word 'dollar' comes from 'thaler', short for joachimsthaler, a silver coin named after the mining valley of Joachimsthal (Jáchymov), in modern Czechia.
Joachimsthal is not in modern Germany, Spain or the Netherlands.
Coins minted at Joachimsthal were called joachimsthalers, shortened to thalers.
The English word dollar developed from thaler, through Low German and Dutch daler.
The Spanish silver dollar (the peso) spread the word dollar internationally.
